decisions.statement: The call a hook judges is read from the payload on standard input.
A refusal is one JSON object on standard output.
A refusal is written to standard error too.
Standing aside says nothing and exits 0.
A payload that will not read is said so and exits 5.
Exiting 5 refuses the call, because the dispatch refuses any exit but 0 or 2.
What is said of a payload that will not read says the call is refused.
The key a hook over a shell command reads that command under is said here alone.
A hook's repository root is walked up to rather than counted in folders.
A refusal names the hook that refused before the refusal says why.
A call handed back with its input changed is one JSON object on standard output.
A call handed back with its input changed exits 0.
A hook changing a call's input is handed the payload whole.
A hook that judges a call reads no field of the payload but the tool input the hook is handed.
A hook that reads its call from the payload is run from here.
Any hook answering that call differently is a hook that has left.
A hook's refusal is handed in as data.
The runner knows only the shape of a judgement rather than the rule any hook judges by.

definition: what a hook reads from the harness and says back to it
